name: University of Chicago Press (books)
description: Book manuscripts for the University of Chicago Press: minimal formatting, headings told apart by size (18, 16 and 14 points, bold), notes made with the word processor's note function, a title page, and Chicago style for references.

source.name: University of Chicago Press, Manuscript Preparation Guidelines
source.notes: The Press page states almost no layout values; confidence is high only for what it states: the heading sizes (a recommendation, given for 12-point text), left-indented extracts, linked notes, the title page, and Chicago style. Two values are not from the Press page but from the Chicago Manual's free Q&A pages, which speak of manuscripts in general: margins of 1 inch ('a typical default setting') and double spacing of everything, 'even notes and block quotations'. Not specified, and taken from the general default: typeface and size, paragraph indent, alignment, hyphenation, alignment and numbering of headings, the block-quotation threshold, the size of notes, position of page numbers (every page must be numbered), running head. The page size is not stated: letter was chosen for a North American publisher. Notes may be footnotes or endnotes (footnotes entered). References may be notes or author-date, not mixed (notes entered; 'chicago-author-date' is the other). Abstracts are to be removed from the chapters of edited volumes, so none is shown. All text goes in one Word file; each table and figure in a file of its own.
